commits.message: An ask whose write throws leaves nothing in flight, and a timeout must be positive and finite (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)
A timed-out ask's late replies reach no later ask, a throwing ask leaves the queue running, and rgba: replies are read (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

A running App asks its terminal, and terminalColors reads its real foreground and background (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

The input parser reads OSC, DCS and APC strings and private-prefix CSI
reports as TerminalReply, never as keys. App.ask writes queries then DA1
and ends answered on DA1's reply, on a timeout, or when the app leaves;
App holds raw mode and the one reader, so the ask adds neither.
terminalColors asks OSC 10/11 and app.terminal draws the next frame on
the answer.

NEL ends a line, and every other C1 control shows a stand-in (rich-control-codes-xh4n.keg) (#537)

* NEL ends a line, and every other C1 control shows a stand-in (rich-control-codes-xh4n.keg)

U+0085 is the one C1 code Unicode gives a meaning in text, a line ending (5.8), so content holds an LF for it and decodeAnsi breaks a capture there. Every other C1 code means nothing in text and Unicode has no picture for it, so content shows U+FFFD, one code unit for one. sealed already keeps every C1 code off the wire. Mojibake repair needs the whole string and is left to the caller.

* A C1 control shows U+2426, one cell under every width setting and no decoding error (rich-control-codes-xh4n.keg)

U+FFFD is East Asian Ambiguous, two cells on a CJK terminal, and indistinguishable
from a real decode error. pictureOf names its ranges and refuses any other, so a
new pictured row cannot inherit a stand-in silently. Stale comments on Disposition
and Pretty's escaping corrected; C1 test titles in hex.

* Each pictured row carries its stand-in, so which code points are pictured has one statement (rich-control-codes-xh4n.keg)

pictureOf reads the row instead of restating its ranges, and a pictured row
cannot be written without a stand-in. The C1 boundary test pins DEL and NBSP
on either side; U+00A0 no longer borders a stripped range.
